text:
emily_support: FYI customer acme-corp hit a ~10m window of 502s from the hosted API around 2026-03-12T16:40Z. They reported a sawtooth pattern — spikes every ~30s. They sent curl logs and trace-ids.

raj_sre: Can you drop one of the trace ids + any envoy upstream IDs? Also which model/route were they hitting?

emily_support: trace_id=tr-9a8b7c, route=/v1/generate (model: open-redwood-3b). Attached snippet from frontdoor logs: 

```
[2026-03-12T16:40:12.123Z] request_id=tr-9a8b7c upstream_reset: stream reset (RST_STREAM), code=2, upstream: auth-proxy:443
[2026-03-12T16:40:12.124Z] envoy response: 502 to client, upstream_status: 502
[2026-03-12T16:40:12.125Z] auth-proxy: token-refresh 500 InternalError (during heartbeat)
```

kevin_platform: Interesting — the timing (every ~30s) matches the tenant auth-heartbeat TTL we added for short-lived tokens. If the auth service has a brief window of degraded capacity when it flushes caches it could reject reauths and cause the frontdoor to return 502s.

linda_oncall: I dug into auth-heartbeat logs for tenant acme-corp: we see a 503 spike at 16:40:11-16:42:00 and a pattern of connection churn where keepalive counts drop to 0 and then bounce back.

emily_support: Customer repro steps: they ran a tight loop of requests with a shared client token; when heartbeat rotated we saw a flurry of backend calls to auth. Repro curl (from their test harness):

```
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n    -H "X-Tenant: acme-corp" \n    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done; wait
```

ci_bot: Automated alert: gateway_502_rate increased by 78% in prod-us-west-2 for route /v1/generate at 2026-03-12T16:40Z.

raj_sre: Quick triage checklist:
- Confirm whether envoy treats auth-proxy as critical (no retry)
- Check per-host connection limits and max_concurrent_streams for auth-proxy cluster
- Look for upstream 5xx or connection reset spikes on auth nodes
- Try a canary rule to add jitter to heartbeat or extend token cache TTL

kevin_platform: I pulled cluster stats from control plane: auth-proxy cluster hit max_connections for a subset of hosts during the interval. max_concurrent_streams was low (100) and many streams were in CLOSE_WAIT, so new streams triggered resets.

linda_oncall: Mitigation applied at 16:46Z: temporarily increased per-host connection limit + bumped max_concurrent_streams to 300 for auth-proxy cluster and enabled short-lived local caching fallback (cache tokens for 60s if auth is flaky). Immediate effect: 502 rate dropped ~80% within 2 minutes.

emily_support: Customer confirmed reduction in errors after that change. They want root cause and long-term fix.

raj_sre: Long-term actions proposed:
1) Add jitter and backoff to auth-heartbeat and avoid synchronized flushes across tenants.
2) Raise default max_concurrent_streams and tune connection pooling for auth-proxy in envoy config.
3) Add a defensive retry/fallback when auth returns 5xx (with strict guardrails to avoid thundering).
4) Run load test to validate auth-proxy under token-rotation churn patterns.
5) Postmortem + coordinator with platform and auth teams.

kevin_platform: I'll create a config candidate and roll to staging. Also want a short simulation harness to reproduce the 30s-sawtooth behavior against a fake auth service that flips into 500s during cache flush.

linda_oncall: Filing an incident (INC-2026-0312-01) and assigning owners: raj_sre (triage), kevin_platform (envoy config), auth-team (heartbeat jitter).

emily_support: Thanks — I'll send the customer a summary and ETA for permanent fixes. Please post any follow-up notes here. :thumbsup:

raj_sre: Follow-up note: we should check whether other tenants with heavy concurrent short-lived tokens show similar patterns; adding to monitoring alert: auth_reauth_rate + upstream_conn_saturation per-tenant.

kevin_platform: Will add metrics and a dashboard widget for conn pool usage.

linda_oncall: Closing the immediate escalation since traffic recovered, but keeping the incident open for follow-ups and postmortem.

emily_support: Acknowledged — customer notified and happy with temporary workaround.
